name: opus_vs_sonnet_conventions_v1
purpose: Option 4 of the R2 discussion: on the tuning-eval cases where R1's novel path still misses a slot, does a stronger model read the slot convention correctly more often than fresh R1 samples? Informs whether building a hidden-like labelled set (option 1) is worth it. Cannot by itself justify adopting R2.
case_selection: every tuning-eval case with a slot miss in run 20261012T051314Z_r1_tuning-eval_S_forced-novel (4 cases, 2 templates: portfolio_single_factor sign convention; two_asset_perfect_correlation_sd variance units). Effective n = 2 conventions.
shared: system prompt, exemplars (S-mode selection), sandbox and max_retries from base_config; prompts identical across arms

arms.name: control_sonnet_medium
arms.why: fresh samples of R1's novel path (R1 used samples 0-4); measures how often a re-draw fixes a case chosen because it failed

arms.name: treatment_opus_medium
arms.why: the stronger model at the same effort

metrics.primary: per-sample correctness of the target slot (official value_matches via score_case on a row holding only that slot), pooled over the 40 samples per arm and reported per template
secondary: per-sample all-fields-correct rate (final and every slot)
per-sample correctness of the non-target fields (regression check)
plurality vote over samples 1-5 and 6-10 of each arm: target-slot correct and all-fields correct (2 votes per case per arm)

interpretation.supports_stronger_model: treatment target-slot rate >= control rate + 0.30 pooled, AND treatment >= control on both templates, AND treatment's non-target-field correct rate is not lower than control's by more than 0.10
interpretation.against: treatment target-slot rate <= control rate + 0.10 pooled
interpretation.caveat: 2 conventions only; anecdotal whatever the outcome; the cases were selected because Sonnet failed, which the control arm accounts for
